nodes.summary: The set of primes $q$ that are not Sophie Germain primes, that is, the primes $q$ for which $2q + 1$ is not prime, is infinite.
nodes.title: Infinitely many primes are not Sophie Germain primes

nodes.summary: A natural number $p$ is a Sophie Germain prime if and only if $p$ is prime and $2p + 1$ is prime.
nodes.title: Characterization of Sophie Germain primes

nodes.summary: Let $a \ge 2$ be a natural number. Then $a$ is a Sophie Germain prime other than $2$ if and only if $(a - 1)! \equiv 2a - 1 \pmod{a(2a + 1)}$ or $(a - 1)! \equiv -(6a + 1) \pmod{a(2a + 1)}$, the congruences being taken in the integers.
nodes.title: Wilson-type characterization of Sophie Germain primes

nodes.summary: A natural number $p$ is a Sophie Germain prime if $p$ is prime and $2p + 1$ is prime. The case $p = 2$ is not excluded.
nodes.title: Sophie Germain primes

nodes.summary: If $p$ is a Sophie Germain prime, then $2p + 1$ is prime.
nodes.title: Safe prime of a Sophie Germain prime

nodes.summary: If $p$ is a Sophie Germain prime, then $p$ is prime.
nodes.title: Sophie Germain primes are prime

nodes.summary: For an odd prime $p$, let $A(p) = \{pr + (p - 1)/2 : r = 1, 2, 3, \dots\}$, and let $A$ be the union of the sets $A(p)$ over all odd primes $p$. A prime is not a Sophie Germain prime if and only if it lies in $A$; equivalently, the Sophie Germain primes are exactly the primes outside $A$.
nodes.title: Primes that are not Sophie Germain primes
